findings.title: retryCount deletion filter is not scoped to SMS and deletes reminders of any method
findings.body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler now includes an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` without a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition (the first branch has it, this one does not). Any WorkflowReminder row whose retryCount exceeds 1 is deleted, regardless of whether it is an EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder. Today only this SMS cron increments retryCount, but any future code path (or a WhatsApp/email retry implementation) that bumps retryCount on a non-SMS reminder will have its rows silently destroyed by the SMS cron job, cancelling reminders that were never related to SMS. The branch should be `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` (and ideally also `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: Database update inside the catch block can itself throw, aborting the entire cron run
findings.body: The new code in the catch block performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before the console.log. If that update throws (e.g., the reminder was concurrently deleted by the deleteMany of an overlapping cron run, or a transient DB error), the exception propagates out of the catch and out of the for-loop, so the handler never sends a response (the caller gets a 500) and all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are not processed in this run. Previously the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not break the loop. The update inside the catch should be wrapped in its own try/catch (or the whole per-reminder processing should be isolated) so a single failure cannot abort the batch.

findings.title: Comment no longer matches what the deleteMany does
findings.body: The comment on line 28 says "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query now also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduled date or method. A maintainer reading the comment will misunderstand the destructive scope of this query; update the comment to reflect both conditions.

findings.title: Reminders dropped after two failures with no logging or record of the loss
findings.body: When the deleteMany removes reminders because retryCount > 1, nothing is logged and no record is kept of which bookings lost their reminders. The per-attempt failures only `console.log` the raw error with no reminder id, so after the row is deleted there is no way to audit that an attendee stopped receiving an SMS reminder. Since two consecutive failures can be caused by a transient Twilio outage (the cron may run every few minutes, so both retries can happen during one incident), reminders can be permanently and silently dropped. At minimum, log the ids/count of deleted retry-exhausted reminders.

findings.title: New retryCount predicate in deleteMany cannot use any existing index
findings.body: The existing indexes on WorkflowReminder are on bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, [method, scheduled, scheduledDate] and [cancelled, scheduledDate]. The added `retryCount > 1` OR-branch matches none of these, so the periodic deleteMany will degrade to a sequential scan over the WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation. As this table accumulates rows over time this adds avoidable load; consider adding an index on retryCount or combining the conditions so the method/scheduledDate index applies.
